questions.explanation:
Answer:(2.) 28, 14, 14 
Solution: 

\tThe leaf tip cells are somatic cells and are diploid (2n), so the chromosome number is 28. 
\tThe middle layer of the anther is also somatic tissue and will have the same chromosome number as other diploid cells, i.e., 28 chromosomes. 
\tThe generative cell is haploid, derived after meiosis of pollen mother cells, so it will have 14 chromosomes. 
\tThe male gametes are formed from the generative cell, and they are also haploid, so they will have 14 chromosomes. 

Thus, the correct sequence is 28, 14, 14

questions.question:
In flowering plants, how many division are required for the formation of mature male gametophyte from microspore mother cell ?
"
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer:3. One meiotic and Two mitotic
Explanation (NCERT-based): 
In flowering plants, the development of the mature male gametophyte (pollen grain) involves the following steps: 
1. Meiotic Division: 

\tThe microspore mother cell (MMC) undergoes meiosis to produce a tetrad of four haploid microspores. 
\tThis is a single meiotic division. 

2. First Mitotic Division: 


\tEach haploid microspore undergoes mitosis to form two cells: 

 A vegetative cell (larger, metabolically active). 
 A generative cell (smaller, which later forms gametes). 
3. Second Mitotic Division: 


\tThe generative cell undergoes one more mitosis to produce two haploid male gametes, completing the development of the mature male gametophyte.

Summary:


\tTotal divisions:
\tOne meiotic division (in MMC).

Thus, the correct answer is One meiotic and Two mitotic.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and select the correct option.
Statement 1 : In insertional inactivation, blue colour produced by bacterial colonies indicate that the vector doesn't have the insert (gene of interest)
Statement 2 : Presence  of insert (gene of interest) results into insertional inactivation of the marker enzyme (β-galactosidase) and colonies do not produce any colour.
"
options: Statement 1 is correct but statement 2 is incorrect
Statement 1 is incorrect but statement 2 is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement 1: 
• In insertional inactivation, if a foreign gene is inserted into a vector (such as a plasmid containing a lacZ gene for β-galactosidase), the function of the β-galactosidase enzyme is disrupted. 
• As a result, bacterial colonies that do not have the insert will produce a blue color in the presence of a substrate like X-gal (which is cleaved by β-galactosidase). Therefore, blue colonies indicate the absence of the insert. 
Statement 2: 
• When the insert (gene of interest) is present, it disrupts the lacZ gene (encoding β-galactosidase), causing the colonies to lose their ability to produce the blue color. These colonies will appear white, indicating that the β-galactosidase enzyme is not functional due to insertional inactivation.
